author: Nekrekid
quote:
O waited over a decade for this. What I got was a game that seems to be more interested in lecturing me than in letting me cause chaos.
Writing: The story feels like it was written by people who dislike the genre they’re working in. Almost every male character is a bumbling, cowardly or cruel caricature, and the women are always the only competent people in the room. GTA has always satirized everyone, but this isn’t satire. It’s one-directional, and it gets old by hour three. The dialogue stops to explain the joke, then explains why the joke is important. I didn’t buy a crime game to be told what to think.Tone: Rockstar used to mock all sides equally. Here the satire has a clear target and a clear moral, which kills the edge that made the series special. Characters who would have been memorable monsters in earlier games are flattened into villains with no charm. The cast needed to be a lot more fun to be around.Performance: 30 fps on a console in 2026 is unacceptable. Driving at speed feels like wading through syrup, and the camera stutters whenever you turn quickly in traffic. The shooting suffers too, because aiming at 30 fps has a noticeable input lag that makes gunfights feel sluggish. A performance mode would have fixed this, but there isn’t one. At this price, 60 fps should be the minimum.Gameplay: Missions follow the usual pattern: drive here, shoot there, follow someone slowly. The map is beautiful, but the activities in it are thin, and the police AI still forgets you the moment you turn a corner.Verdict: A gorgeous world wasted on a preachy script and a frame rate that holds back everything else. Wait for a sale, and for a patch that unlocks 60 fps.This is a fictional review written in the voice of an annoyed player, not a description of the real game. I can write a version with a different tone, make it shorter, or format it as a Steam review.
